programme.title: Inglourious Basterds

programme.title: Crawlspace

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v USA (Kick-off 3.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the Group D match at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA. The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. With analysis from Juan Mata, Ange Postecoglu and Bradley Wright-Phillips, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon

programme.desc: Norway v France (Kick-off 8.00pm). All the action from the final match in Group I for both teams, held at Boston Stadium in the USA. This is the first meeting between the nations since 2014, when France prevailed 4-0 in a friendly. The French are likely to go into this fixture as favourites to win once again, but a closer contest is anticipated. Should they both be available, the game could see two of the world's leading forwards go head to head in Frenchman Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland, and it would be little surprise if either one of them proved to be the difference-maker this evening. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Uruguay v Spain (Kick-off 1.00am). Laura Woods presents coverage of the third and final match in Group H for both teams, held at Guadalajara Stadium in Mexico. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. Spain picked up a much-needed win in their last game against Saudi Arabia thanks to a 4-0 victory, a result that puts them top of the table going into this match. Uruguay were held by Cape Verde in a 2-2 draw in their previous match, but still stand second in the group at this point. With analysis from Gary Neville, Juan Mata and Ange Postecoglou

programme.title: FIFA WC2026: Panama v England
programme.desc: Panama v England (Kick-off 10.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group L match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA, as the two sides play their final group game. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia. With analysis from Roy Keane, Ian Wright and Gary Neville, pitchside inserts from Laura Woods, Emma Hayes and Karen Carney, commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, and reports from Gabriel Clarke

The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. Spain picked up a much-needed win in their last game against Saudi Arabia thanks to a 4-0 victory, a result that puts them top of the table going into this match. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia. The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia. The USA have already won the group and will play in the last 32 on Wednesday in Santa Clara, while Türkiye have already been eliminated following defeats to Australia and Paraguay. Four of the five previous meetings between these nations have taken place since the turn of the century, and all of them have ended in a 2-1 scoreline. Two were in favour of the Americans, and the other two went the way of the Turkish, including the most recent encounter in June last year, when Arda Güler and Kerem Aktürko?lu were on the scoresheet in East Hartford, Connecticut. While the Crescent-Stars haven't appeared at a World Cup since 2002, the Americans had two group-stage matches against European opposition four years ago, beginning their campaign with a 1-1 draw against Wales that saw Gareth Bale equalise late on from the penalty spot after Timothy Weah had given USMNT the lead in the first half, before they moved on to play England in their second game, which ended in a drab 0-0 draw. These two came into the tournament as the favourites to progress to the knockout rounds, but even if both teams' progression is already guaranteed, they will be eager to make a statement against strong opposition and look to top the group. The nations last met in the group stage of the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, when first-half goals by Pedro and Roberto Soldado gave the Spaniards a 2-1 win. That was a match between the reigning European and South American champions at the time, and coming into this encounter Spain are European champions once more after they won that title two years ago, while Uruguay were third in the most recent Copa America held in the United States in 2024. Spain picked up a much-needed win in their last game against Saudi Arabia thanks to a 4-0 victory, a result that puts them top of the table going into this match. programme.desc: Panama v England (Kick-off 10.00pm). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group L match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA, as the two sides play their final group game. This is just the second-ever meeting between the two countries, with the first coming in the group stage of the 2018 World Cup in Russia. That game was a memorable one for the Three Lions as they brushed their opponents aside with a 6-1 victory. Braces from Harry Kane and John Stones, as well as a goal from Jesse Lingard, gave England a 5-0 lead at half-time before Kane completed his hat-trick in the second period. Panama did create some history in the second half as they scored their first-ever goal at the World Cup finals thanks to a consolation finish from Felipe Baloy. The Three Lions will be hoping to finish top of this group with victory here after they missed their chance to progress to the knock-out stages in their last game against Ghana, as they were held to a 0-0 draw by the African country. Panama are already out of the competition after two 1-0 defeats by Ghana and Croatia. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Ivory Coast v Group I runner-up (Kick-off 6.00pm). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Dallas Stadium in the USA. Ivory Coast finished second in Group E on six points, just losing out on top spot due to their head-to-head record against group winners Germany. Despite that they still created history after they reached the knock-out stages for the first time, something they hadn't done in their previous three attempts. Group I saw Norway and France claim victories in their first two matches, with star strikers Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe impressing

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Group I winner v Group C/D/F/G/H third-placed team (Kick-off 10.00pm). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. France were the pre-tournament favourites to top Group I, and they won their opening two matches 3-1 against Senegal and Iraq. However, Norway also had six points from their first two games and will have pipped the French to top spot should they have defeated them. Whoever won the group will fancy their chances against whichever third-place team they face, but can take nothing for granted in a competition in which many upsets have occurred over the years

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Mexico v Group C/E/F/H/I third-placed team (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the round-of-32 match at Mexico City Stadium. Co-hosts Mexico beat South Africa, South Korea and Czechia in their Group A matches, without conceding a goal, and have an outstanding record here in their spiritual home. There is a scenario would see the Mexicans on a collision course with England, should Thomas Tuchel's men top their group and progress to the last 16, but Mexico will simply be focused on victory here first, against a third-placed qualifier
